summary: I measured the file:// constraints in Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 instead of relying on folklore. Both block fetch, XHR, ES modules (static and dynamic import()), file-based Workers, Service Workers, iframe DOM access, cssRules on linked stylesheets, and canvas export after drawing a local . Classic

libraries.name: Observable Framework
libraries.capabilities: Static-site generator for data apps; data loaders in any language (x.json.py -> stdout) run at build and write static snapshots; FileAttachment; build cache; build fails on loader error
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - output uses ES modules + fetch(FileAttachment); needs HTTP. Not usable from file://
libraries.reason: Best precedent for build-time data loaders (naming, stdout contract, caching, fail-fast). But deploy is deprecated, Observable Cloud hosting ended 2025-10, development moved to Notebook Kit 2.x, and the output is ESM. Borrow the conventions, not the tool.

libraries.name: Evidence
libraries.capabilities: SQL + Markdown BI-as-code; named query results bound to components via props (<BarChart data={q} x= y= series=/>); classic build = SvelteKit static + parquet + DuckDB-WASM
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - SvelteKit/ESM + DuckDB-WASM; the 2026 docs describe `evidence serve` and Studio and list no static build command
libraries.reason: Authoring model (SQL + markdown + props-as-bindings) is worth copying; the packaging is not file://-compatible and the product has moved toward a served model.

libraries.name: Quarto dashboards
libraries.license: MIT (CLI; bundles Pandoc GPL as separate binary)
libraries.capabilities: Pandoc-based dashboards: pages/rows/columns, cards, tabsets, sidebars, toolbars, value boxes; static or Shiny-backed; embed-resources:true for single-file HTML
libraries.offline_classic_script: Only in single-file/static-widget form (embed-resources); OJS/Shiny need runtime/server
libraries.reason: Good layout vocabulary (cards, value boxes, sidebars) and a clear static-vs-server split; single-file mode is a precedent for our --single-file option. Not a runtime dependency.

libraries.name: Vega-Lite (+ vega, vega-embed)
libraries.capabilities: Declarative JSON grammar: data (values/url/named), top-level datasets, mark, encoding channels, transforms, params/selections (point/interval, bind to legend/scales/inputs); runtime data swap via view.insert/change
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes - UMD build/vega.min.js (175 KB gz) + build/vega-lite.min.js (79 KB gz) + build/vega-embed.min.js (20 KB gz)
libraries.interactions_animation: Selections, brushing, zoom/pan via bound scales; limited animation
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, theta, radius, strokeDash, detail, text, tooltip, lat/long, facet
libraries.reason: Use its encoding vocabulary and $schema-URL versioning in our spec. Optionally ship a 'vega-lite' component so power users or an LLM can paste specs. ECharts remains the main renderer for pitchbook look and size.

libraries.name: Altair + vl-convert
libraries.capabilities: Python API emitting Vega-Lite JSON; chart.save('x.html', inline=True) inlines JS (requires vl-convert); chart.save('x.json') spec-only; browserless SVG/PNG/PDF via vl-convert
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes when saved inline (HTML embeds the JS)
libraries.reason: Shows the 'spec is the artifact' pattern from Python and the inline-vs-CDN trade-off. Not needed in our stack.

libraries.name: Perspective
libraries.capabilities: WASM streaming query engine + virtual data grid, pivot, WebGL charts as a custom element; viewer config save()/restore() JSON; Arrow interchange; Python/Node/Rust servers
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - dist/cdn/perspective.js is ESM using import.meta.url and fetch(*.wasm), plus workers (verified)
libraries.reason: Its serializable view-state JSON is a good precedent for 'saved views'. Blocked on file:// (ESM + WASM fetch + workers); only viable in a hosted/API mode.

libraries.name: Datapane
libraries.capabilities: Python -> standalone HTML reports
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (inlined HTML)
libraries.reason: Officially 'no longer actively maintained'; the final release only kept local report saving. A cautionary tale about building on a vendor-led report SDK.

libraries.name: Panel / Bokeh
libraries.capabilities: save(resources=INLINE) standalone HTML; document JSON in <script type=application/json>; embed=True precomputes widget states (~1000 max, 3 options per slider by default)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes inline (bokeh.min.js 1.39 MB classic); embedded states exported as JSON files need HTTP (docs: 'Browsers block access to local files')
libraries.interactions_animation: jslink/embedded states; full interactivity needs a server
libraries.reason: Confirms the file:// diagnosis. Precomputed-state embedding explodes combinatorially, so ship data plus a client query engine instead.

libraries.name: Plotly (plotly.js / plotly.py write_html / Kaleido)
libraries.capabilities: Figure JSON = {data, layout, config, frames}; write_html include_plotlyjs True|'cdn'|'directory'|path|False; v4 removed mapbox traces and MathJax 2
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes - plotly.min.js UMD (4.7 MB raw / 1.44 MB gz)
libraries.reason: include_plotlyjs='directory' is the exact precedent for a shared vendor/ next to index.html, and the data/layout/config split is clean. Too heavy (4x ECharts) and less pitchbook-like to adopt.

libraries.name: Streamlit / stlite
libraries.capabilities: Python app server with WebSocket reruns; stlite runs it in Pyodide (WASM) and fetches wheels
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - needs a server (Streamlit) or fetch/WASM (stlite)
libraries.reason: Its rerun-on-widget-change server model is the opposite of a static deliverable.

libraries.name: Apache Superset
libraries.capabilities: BI server; embedded dashboards via guest tokens
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - server required
libraries.reason: Not static. Its chart 'form data' JSON is only a reference for portable chart definitions.

libraries.name: Metabase
libraries.capabilities: BI server; embedding
libraries.offline_classic_script: No
libraries.reason: AGPL plus a server-only model; unsuitable for client deliverables.

libraries.name: Rill
libraries.capabilities: BI-as-code: YAML metrics views (dimensions, measures with expression + format_preset/format_d3, valid_percent_of_total) and YAML canvas dashboards (rows/items/width, tabs, pinned/required filters)
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - Go server + DuckDB/ClickHouse
libraries.reason: Its metrics-layer vocabulary (measure formats, percent-of-total validity) and YAML authoring should inform our field metadata and the analyst-facing YAML.

libraries.name: Graphic Walker / PyGWalker
libraries.capabilities: Tableau-like drag-and-drop explorer; IChart spec {encodings: rows, columns, color, opacity, size, shape, theta, radius, longitude, latitude, geoId, details, filters, text}; $schema stamp + spec.migrate(); PyGWalker to_html (browser computation only)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Partial - graphic-walker.umd.js (4.1 MB, 1.18 MB gz) expects React>=19, ReactDOM, styled-components globals; React 19.3.0 ships no UMD (verified)
libraries.reason: Copy its channel list and spec versioning for our self-service mode. Embedding it is impractical: React 19 has no UMD and the bundle is heavy.

libraries.name: Great Tables
libraries.capabilities: Publication tables from pandas/polars: header, spanners, stub, row groups, summary rows, footnotes (opt_footnote_spec), source notes; fmt_number/currency/percent/engineering/number_si/fraction/duration/date, data_color, nanoplots, define_units; opt_interactive (0.24); gtsave via headless Chrome; HTML-escaping by default since 1.0
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (Python); emits static HTML with inline CSS
libraries.reason: The best reference for table anatomy and formatter vocabulary, which our JS table spec should mirror. Could also produce static tables for PDF/email on the builder side, but it puts data into HTML, so it is not the primary path.

libraries.name: Frictionless Table Schema / Data Package v2 (+ frictionless-py)
libraries.capabilities: Field types (string, number, integer, date, datetime, year, yearmonth, duration, geopoint, geojson, list, any), constraints, categories (+labels, ordered), labelled missingValues, primaryKey/uniqueKeys/foreignKeys, fieldsMatch, $schema, version, sources[].version
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (spec); JS libs tableschema 1.12.6 / datapackage 1.1.10 stale since 2022
libraries.reason: Adopt its vocabulary as the base of rk.dataset@1 (aligned with pandas orient='table') and validate in Python with frictionless-py. Extend it with unit, format, role and aggregate.

libraries.name: JSON Schema 2020-12 (+ python jsonschema / pydantic)
libraries.capabilities: Contract and spec validation; pydantic models -> model_json_schema() -> schemas/*.json shipped with the kit; drives LLM-safe editing in step 2
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (builder-side)
libraries.reason: Gives one source of truth for the data contract and report spec, with fail-fast builds and validated LLM edits later. 2020-12 is still the current dialect.

libraries.name: pandas to_json(orient='table')
libraries.capabilities: Emits {schema:{fields, primaryKey, pandas_version:'1.4.0'}, data:[...]}; categoricals -> type any + constraints.enum; NaN -> null
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: Zero-effort ingestion path for analysts. Gotchas (verified on 3.0.5): pass date_format='iso' because epoch is deprecated; ISO datetimes have no Z; extDtype must be stripped.

libraries.name: Mosaic (UW IDL)
libraries.capabilities: Coordinated views over DuckDB; declarative JSON/YAML spec (meta, data, params, vconcat/hconcat, plot, input) with $param references; Selection.intersect/union/single/crossfilter
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - requires DuckDB (WASM or server)
libraries.reason: Adopt its selection-resolution semantics: under crossfilter a component's own clause does not filter itself. Also its $param syntax for our spec.

libraries.name: Grafana dashboard JSON model (schema v2)
libraries.license: AGPL-3.0 (code; the concept is free to emulate)
libraries.capabilities: v1: panels[] with gridPos on a 24-column grid and schemaVersion migrations; v2: spec.elements map + layout kinds (Grid/AutoGrid/Rows/Tabs) whose items reference elements
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: Separating elements from layout, plus schemaVersion migrations, is the right shape for our report spec. Do not reuse its code (AGPL).

libraries.name: Flourish templates (SDK)
libraries.license: Proprietary SDK license (SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md)
libraries.capabilities: Templates declare data-binding slots (single column vs multi-column), so users map their own columns to visual roles
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: The binding-slot concept fits a future 'client maps their own columns' feature. The license is not OSI, so use the concept only.

libraries.capabilities: dataset.source + series.encode bind columns to dimensions; dataset transforms; SVG renderer; server-side renderToSVGString + ssr/client hydration (3.6 KB UMD)

libraries.capabilities: Sorted-index multidimensional filtering and group reductions for linked views
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes - crossfilter.min.js UMD (global crossfilter)

libraries.capabilities: Arrow IPC read/write, columnar tables
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes - Arrow.es2015.min.js UMD (global Arrow)
libraries.reason: For the future API mode with large datasets (Accept: Arrow stream). On file://, Arrow IPC can be shipped base64-encoded inside a .js file.

libraries.name: DuckDB-WASM
libraries.capabilities: Full SQL in browser over parquet/arrow/csv
libraries.offline_classic_script: No - ESM + Worker + WASM fetch, all blocked on file:// (verified class of failures)

libraries.name: Paged.js
libraries.capabilities: Polyfill for CSS Paged Media (margin boxes, running headers, page counters)
libraries.offline_classic_script: UMD exists, but on file:// it XHRs linked stylesheets and fails (verified in Chromium 156 and Firefox 157); works only with inline <style>
libraries.reason: Stale stable release and broken on file:// with linked CSS. Chrome/Edge 131+ margin boxes plus DOM-rendered slide footers cover the need.

libraries.name: Vivliostyle core
libraries.capabilities: CSS typesetting / paged media engine
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: AGPL license is not acceptable for client deliverables.

libraries.name: Playwright (Python)
libraries.capabilities: Headless Chromium/Firefox/WebKit; page.pdf(prefer_css_page_size, print_background, outline, tagged); per-slide PNG screenshots; file:// regression tests
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (builder/CI)
libraries.reason: One engine for PDF, PNG and automated file:// tests, identical to what clients run. Verified: 960x540 pt pages, outline bookmarks, and beforeprint firing during page.pdf. In Firefox tests, re-enable strict_origin_policy.

libraries.name: WeasyPrint
libraries.capabilities: HTML/CSS to PDF with good paged-media support
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (Python); does not execute JavaScript
libraries.reason: Without JavaScript, charts and dynamic tables would need pre-rendering. Playwright covers the same need with the real runtime.

key_insights: file:// behaviour measured in Chromium 156 and stock Firefox 157. BLOCKED: fetch/XHR of local JSON,

Test-harness trap: Playwright's bundled Firefox sets security.fileuri.strict_origin_policy=false in playwright.cfg, so fetch, modules and workers appear to work on file://. CI must pass firefox_user_prefs={'security.fileuri.strict_origin_policy': True}.

Data transport: write data/<id>.json (canonical, for HTTP/API) and data/<id>.js = RK.data.register(id, JSON.parse("...")) from the same serialized string. Lazy-load per page via script injection; never assign globals.

Benchmark (40k rows x 15 fields, file://, median of 5). Chromium: records literal 372 ms vs JSON.parse 133 ms; columns literal 110 ms vs JSON.parse 79 ms. Firefox: 411/220/177/160 ms. Sizes: records 9.3 MB vs columns 5.8 MB; gzipped 3.08 vs 2.28 MB. Use JSON.parse above 10 kB (V8 guidance) and offer orient:'columns'.

Python serialization gotchas: json.dumps(NaN) emits 'NaN', which is invalid JSON and makes JSON.parse throw, so map NaN/Inf to null + flag and dump with allow_nan=False. pandas 3 to_json without date_format warns that epoch is deprecated. orient='table' datetimes have no Z, so new Date() parses date-only strings as UTC but datetime strings as local time, which can shift days. Make 'date' values YYYY-MM-DD strings parsed without timezone conversion.

Contract = Frictionless Table Schema v2 names (fields, type, format, constraints, categories, labelled missingValues, primaryKey) plus finance extensions: unit {currency, scale, kind}, Excel-style format, role (key/label/dimension/measure/time/geo.*), default aggregate (multiples default to median, never sum), polarity, cell flags[] linked to footnotes, meta.source[]/footnotes[]/asOf/lineage, version + sha256 hash, orient records|columns|rows.

Spec shape: components{} map (elements) separate from pages[].items[] grid placement that references them (Grafana schema v2). Bindings use Vega-Lite / Graphic Walker channel names (x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, theta, radius, latitude, longitude, geoId, detail, label, tooltip) and compile to ECharts dataset/encode/visualMap. Params use $name; selections use Mosaic resolution (crossfilter: a component's own clause never filters itself).

Versioning: $schema + specVersion with migration chains in both JS and Python (Vega-Lite, Grafana schemaVersion, Graphic Walker IChart.$schema + migrate()). Datasets carry contract tag, version and hash; manifest carries client revision, changelog, generator/kit versions and file checksums. Each delivered folder freezes its own kit + vendor copies (Plotly include_plotlyjs='directory' precedent) so it renders identically years later.

Print: 1280x720 CSS px = 13.333in x 7.5in = PowerPoint 16:9. With @page{size:13.333in 7.5in; margin:0} Chromium produced exact 960x540 pt pages, so fixed-geometry slides need no print-time chart resize, and Ctrl+P works without beforeprint timing hacks.

PDF evidence: ECharts canvas charts become raster images (560x360 at DPR1 in headless) with no selectable text; the SVG renderer stays vector with extractable labels. Default to SVG for report charts; use canvas plus devicePixelRatio 2-3 only for dense series.

beforeprint and matchMedia('print') change events fire during headless page.pdf(), but the builder should still call RK.print.prepare() explicitly (animation:false, resize, invalidateSize) and await document.fonts.ready.

Browser support (MDN BCD 8.1.5): @page size in Chrome 15, Firefox 95, Safari 18.2; page margin boxes only in Chrome/Edge 131+ (not Firefox or Safari). Render footers, page numbers and confidentiality lines in the DOM with CSS counters and treat margin boxes as an enhancement. print-color-adjust unprefixed needs Chrome 136+, so also emit -webkit-print-color-adjust.
On-screen scaling of fixed slides: transform: scale(k) kept ECharts 6.1 hover and Leaflet 1.9.4 clicks correct in both browsers. CSS zoom:0.6 made ECharts report the wrong bar in both, so avoid zoom.
Paged.js 0.4.3 (last stable 2023) fails on file:// when print CSS is a <link> (it XHRs the stylesheet) but runs with inline <style>; do not depend on it. Vivliostyle is AGPL; avoid.

Avoid as runtime deps on file://: Perspective (moved to @perspective-dev 5.6.0; ESM + import.meta.url + WASM fetch), DuckDB-WASM (npm latest is a dev build; needs workers + WASM), Graphic Walker (UMD needs React 19 globals; React 19.3.0 ships no UMD), Observable Framework/Notebook Kit and Evidence output (ESM + fetch; Framework's deploy deprecated, Evidence docs now centre on `evidence serve`), Datapane (unmaintained since 0.17.0, 2023-09).

Single-file mode (--single-file) for email or portal upload: inline CSS/JS, datasets as <script type='application/json' id='rk-data-<id>'>, fonts and images as base64; escape '<' as <. Precedents: Quarto embed-resources, Plotly include_plotlyjs=True, Altair inline=True, Bokeh INLINE. HTML attachments are often blocked by gateways (HTML smuggling), so the default delivery is a zipped folder plus PDF via data room.

Chrome shares one localStorage bucket across all file:// pages, so namespace keys rk:<report.id>:<revision>: and keep only UI state there. HTML-escape all data text by default (Great Tables 1.0 made escaping its default) and allow a safe markdown subset.

Great Tables 1.0 (2026-09-25) is the table-anatomy reference for our table spec: title/subtitle, spanners, stub + row groups with indentation, summary_rows, cell-targeted footnotes, source notes, sub_missing, fmt_* incl. number_si/engineering/fraction, data_color, nanoplots, define_units.

Builder pipeline borrowed from Observable Framework: loaders/<id>.json.py writes to stdout (logs to stderr), non-zero exit fails the build, outputs are cached by loader + input hash, and only datasets referenced by the spec are built. Analysts write df.to_json(orient='table', date_format='iso') plus a <id>.meta.yaml sidecar for titles, units, formats, sources and footnotes.

Step-2 readiness: JSON Schema (from pydantic) for spec and contract lets a local LLM propose JSON Patches or formulas that are validated before apply. Field description/unit/role/aggregate double as a semantic layer (Rill metrics-view idea). A local LLM endpoint called from file:// is a cross-origin request from origin null, so the server must allow CORS (*/null).
